vulnerability.title: Django URL resolver accepts endpoint paths with a trailing newline because '$' matches before a final newline, allowing a bypass of upstream path-based access control
vulnerability.category_l2: trailing-newline URL path bypass of an upstream path-based access control due to dollar-anchored endpoints applied with re.search

critical_operation.description: RegexPattern.match applies the endpoint regex with re.search (line 156). Endpoint patterns are generated by _route_to_regex with a trailing '$' (line 243 of the 3.0.2 file, inside _route_to_regex), and re_path() patterns written by applications commonly end in '$' too. In Python's re module '$' matches at the end of the string or immediately before a newline at the end, so '/articles/2003/\n' matches '^articles/(?P<year>[0-9]{4})/$' and is resolved; the unresolved '\n' is returned as the remaining path at line 165 and discarded by an endpoint. A request carrying a percent-encoded trailing newline in PATH_INFO therefore reaches a view that an upstream proxy or access-control layer matching the raw URL path would not have allowed through. The fix makes endpoint patterns ending in '$' use self.regex.fullmatch(path) (3.1.14 line 157) and emits r'\Z' instead of '$' from _route_to_regex (3.1.14 line 247); fullmatch alone rejects the trailing newline because it requires the whole string to be consumed.

entry_point.description: BaseHandler._get_response passes request.path_info to resolver.resolve(). path_info derives from the WSGI PATH_INFO, in which a percent-encoded newline is decoded to '\n', so an HTTP client can place a trailing newline in the path that the URL resolver sees.

trace.description: resolver_match = resolver.resolve(request.path_info) hands the decoded path, potentially ending in a newline, to the URL resolver
URLResolver.resolve delegates to self.pattern.match(path) for each URLPattern
re.search accepts a '$'-anchored endpoint match that stops before a trailing newline, so the URL resolves
endpoint patterns are generated with a trailing '$', which is the anchor that re.search lets match before a final newline
the unconsumed '\n' is returned as the remaining path; an endpoint pattern ignores it and reports a successful match

source_crosscheck.notes: The CNA (mitre) gives the affected versions and description but no CVSS and no CWE. NVD supplies its own Primary CVSS 3.1 7.3 HIGH and NVD-CWE-Other, so it is an independent assessment. OSV repeats the same CVSS 3.1 vector and adds a CVSS 4.0 vector, but sets its database severity to MODERATE and assigns CWE-287; Django's own release notes call the issue 'low'. The published severity levels therefore do not agree (HIGH vs MODERATE vs low), and the affected-range lower bound for the 3.x line differs: the CNA text and NVD CPE start at 3.1, while OSV starts at 3.0a1. The git evidence shows the same vulnerable code at 3.0.2, 3.0.14 and 3.1.13, and the fix only on the branches that received a release, so the snapshot is affected at the code level even though 3.0.x is absent from the CNA/NVD range text and had no fixed release.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read django/urls/resolvers.py at 3.0.2 and confirm RegexPattern.match applies the endpoint regex with re.search and that _route_to_regex appends '$'.
An independent reviewer must confirm that request.path_info can carry a trailing newline and that the resolved view is reached while an upstream path-based control would not allow it.
An independent reviewer must confirm the backports 22bd1748/333c6560/7cf7d74e are the fixes, that 3.1.14/3.2.10/2.2.25 contain them, and that 3.0.14 is still unfixed.

An independent reviewer must resolve the published severity conflict (NVD HIGH 7.3 vs GHSA MODERATE vs Django 'low') and the 3.0.x affected-range difference; severity_consistent must be false if the levels are not reconciled.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No code was executed and no HTTP request was made: the trailing-newline acceptance is read from the regex semantics, the resolver code and the regression test, not reproduced.

The CNA text and NVD CPE do not list a 3.0.x range; only OSV does (introduced 3.0a1). The snapshot is treated as affected because the vulnerable code is identical at 3.0.2 and 3.1.13 and 3.0.14 is still unfixed, but the published range text disagrees.
The published severity levels conflict: NVD HIGH 7.3, GHSA MODERATE, Django release notes 'low'. No level was chosen by coercion; the dossier records the NVD level and the conflict.

Exploitability depends on a deployment that puts a path-based access control in front of Django and on that layer disagreeing about the trailing-newline path; the library-level defect is that the resolver accepts such a path.

The 3.0.x line never received a fixed release (3.0.14 still carries blob 19d0d989), so users of this snapshot must upgrade to 3.1.14/3.2.10 or later; the dataset records the flaw at 3.0.2 without a same-line fixed release.
The mainline fix commit d4dcd5b9 is used only for the diff and release notes; the 4.0.1 release tag was not fetched, so the 4.0 fix is not content-verified here.
The advisory gives no reporter or reproduction reference beyond the oss-security post, so no independent reproduction is available and grade A is not attainable.
open_questions: Which WSGI servers and proxies normalize or reject percent-encoded newlines in PATH_INFO differently was not surveyed; the advisory's bypass premise depends on that difference.

Whether the CNA intentionally omitted 3.0.x because it was end-of-life, rather than because the code was unaffected, is not stated; OSV's range and the code identity point to affected but unsupported.
Whether any 3.0.x downstream backport added the same fix without an upstream tag was not checked.
